# **Data Import and Cleaning**    

### Load in libraries :)
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(readxl)
theme_set(theme_cowplot())
library(factoextra)
library(wesanderson)
library(gt)
library(openxlsx)
library(nlme)
library(lmtest)
library(AICcmodavg)
library(lattice)
library(chemhelper) #for retention index calculations
library(janitor)
library(snakecase)
pal <- wes_palette(name = "Zissou1")
```

### Read in the data!
```{r}
phyto_dat <- read.csv("phytoncide_dat")

phyto_dat$brand <- factor(phyto_dat$brand)
phyto_dat$location <- factor(phyto_dat$location)

glimpse(phyto_dat)

pump_dat <- read_xlsx("uw_test_field_sheet_oct_2026.xlsx", sheet = "tidy") |>
  select(c(location, pump, cubic_m))
glimpse(pump_dat)
```

#Joining on the shared columns
```{r}
dat_joined <- left_join(phyto_dat, pump_dat, by=join_by(pump,location)) 
#joined on the shared columns

glimpse(dat_joined)
```

#correcting concentrations with volume
```{r}
dat <- dat_joined |>
  mutate(conc_ngcm = amount/cubic_m,
         conc_ugcm = conc_ngcm/1000)
```

#calculating LOD
```{r}
compound_info <- read_xlsx("compound_summary_table_info_2024.xlsx") |>
  mutate(lod = (3*concentration_ion)/(ion_signal/ion_noise),
         loq = (10*concentration_ion)/(ion_signal/ion_noise),
         lod_old = (3*concentration)/(signal/noise),
         loq_old = (10*concentration)/(signal/noise))

#the old LOD/LOQ was done in undergrad and I have gone through it again to make sure I understand it now and have adjusted it with how I would do it now since I have learned more.
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tbl-cap: "LOD/LOQ of Compounds"

lodq <- compound_info |>
  subset(select = c(name, lod, loq))

lodq |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "LOD/LOQ of Compounds") |>
  cols_label(name = "Compound",
             lod = "LOD",
             loq = "LOQ") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(lod, loq),
             decimals = 3)|>
  opt_row_striping()
```

# Retention Index Calculations

Retention indexes are calcuated by using the retention time of alkanes that proceed directly before and after the compound.The equation is as follows

> Ix = 100n + 100(tx-tn) / (tn+1 − tn)

The package I would like to use for this is: chemhelper by Eric R. Scott

To cite package ‘chemhelper’ in publications use:

Scott E (2023). chemhelper: Helper Functions For Dealing With GCMS and LCMS data from IonAnalytics. R package version 0.0.0.9000, https://github.com/aariq/chemhelper.


Getting just the retention times and compound names from the compound info table. These retention times are what the method used to find the compounds:
```{r}
xrt <- compound_info |>
  subset(select = c(name, rt)) |>
  mutate(name = to_snake_case(name)) #converting names to snakecase

nrt <- read_xlsx("Alkane_RT.xlsx") # reading in alkane rt info

xrt <- xrt|>
  mutate(ri = calc_RI(rt, nrt$rt, nrt$carbon_num)) 

#so now xrt has the RI calculations for our compounds
```

# trimming the tibble so I have less anxiety looking at it
```{r}
dat_smol <- dat |>
  select(type, pump, brand, location, sample_id, peak_name, retention_time, amount, peak_area, conc_ugcm, conc_ngcm) |>
  unite(id, pump, brand, location, sep = "_", remove = FALSE)
```

# General visualization of data
```{r}
dat_sum <- dat_smol |>
  group_by(brand, location, type, peak_name) |>
  summarise(conc_mean = mean(conc_ugcm),
            conc_stdv = sd(conc_ugcm),
            n = n()
            )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tbl-cap: "General Summary Table"

dat_sum |>
  filter_out(type == "control") |>
  filter_out(conc_mean == 0) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(title = "General Summary (ug/m^3)")|>
  fmt_number(columns = c(conc_mean, conc_stdv),
             decimals = 3)|>
  opt_row_striping()
```

# Comparing forest SKC and Gilair
```{r}
forest_comp <- dat_smol|>
  filter(location == "forest") |>
  filter_out(type == "control") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(peak_name, conc_ugcm, median),
    y = conc_ugcm,
    fill = brand)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme( axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 90)) +
  labs(title = "Comparing gilair and skc in Forest",
       x = "Compound Name",
       y = "Concentration (ug/m^3)")

forest_comp
```

# Comparing city skc and gilair
```{r}
city_comp <- dat_smol|>
  filter(location == "urban") |>
  filter_out(type == "control") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(peak_name, conc_ugcm, median),
    y = conc_ugcm,
    fill = brand)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme( axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 90)) +
  labs(title = "Comparing gilair and skc in Urban",
       x = "Compound Name",
       y = "Concentration (ug/m^3)")

city_comp
```

# Pooling both skc and gilair to get an idea of forest vs urban
```{r}
location_comp <- dat_smol |>
  filter(type != "control") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = forcats::fct_reorder(peak_name, conc_ugcm, median),
    y = conc_ugcm,
    fill = location)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  theme( axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 90)) +
  labs(title = "Comparing locations",
       x = "Compound Name",
       y = "Concentration (ug/m^3)")

location_comp
```

# Trying a quick heatmap???
```{r}
heat_map <- dat_smol |>
  filter(type != "control") |>
  ggplot(aes(id, forcats::fct_reorder(peak_name, conc_ugcm, mean), fill = log10(conc_ugcm + 0.001))) +
  geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    direction = 1,
    name = "log10(conc)"
  ) +
   theme( axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 45, )) +
    labs(title = "Heatmap",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Compound")

heat_map
```

# export for metaboanalyst
```{r}
uw_metabo <- dat_smol |>
  filter(type != "control") |>
  select(location, peak_name, id, conc_ugcm) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = peak_name, values_from = conc_ugcm)

write.xlsx(uw_metabo, "uw_metabo_1.xlsx")
 
  
```
